items.excerpt:
OEMpocalypse Part 2: Rooting Samsung Flagships via Knox DualDAR
Calif Research 发布 OEMpocalypse 系列第二篇，通过 Knox DualDAR 的 confused-deputy 漏洞与内核驱动页 UAF 组成两阶段利用链，从零权限应用在 Galaxy S23、S26 EU、S26 US 和 S26 Ultra 四款机型上高可靠获取 root。
作者亲历复现并披露完整漏洞细节，读者可了解 OEM 驱动漏洞链如何绕过 RKP 等多层防御获取 root。
把 OEMpocalypse 策略用到三星 Knox DualDAR 上：一个 confused-deputy 沙箱逃逸加上一个页 UAF，就能让不受信任的应用在 Galaxy S23 和 S26 上拿到 root。
在 第一部分 中，我介绍了 OEMpocalypse 策略：利用内核驱动中某个 OEM 特有的页释放后使用（UAF）漏洞；当 SELinux 限制对该驱动的访问时，先利用一个 OEM 特有的沙箱逃逸。本文把这一策略应用到三星的 Knox DualDAR——一项在 Android 基于文件的加密之上再对文件加密的企业功能。第一阶段利用 DualDAR 系统服务中的 confused deputy，加载一个原生库，从而在其高权限加密守护进程中实现代码执行。这让我得以访问内核驱动，第二阶段便在那里利用一个页 UAF。该驱动释放一个物理页，却仍把它映射在用户空间，于是留下一个可读可写的别名指向已释放内存。我在一台用 Magisk 取得 root 的 Galaxy S23 上开发了这条利用链，并移植到未改动、引导程序锁定的 Galaxy S26 EU、S26 US 和 S26 Ultra 设备上。在全部四台测试设备上，这条链都能从一个零权限应用出发，以很高的可靠性拿到 root 。
图 1：在引导程序锁定的 Galaxy S26 EU 和 S26 Ultra 上完整跑通三星利用链。
披露时间线： 我于 2026 年 6 月 17 日向三星报告。Bug 1 在 2026 年 8 月的版本中修复，Bug 2 在 2026 年 9 月的版本中修复，编号为 CVE-2026-21102 / SVE-2026-3092 。
Android 通过三层机制在整个系统中实施沙箱隔离：Unix 自主访问控制（DAC）、SELinux 以及 seccomp 。对普通的第三方应用而言，这通常意味着每个应用拥有独立的 UID、一个 untrusted_app SELinux 域（或其针对特定 API 级别的变体），以及一个 seccomp 过滤器。这些层共同界定了进程的攻击面，包括它对文件系统、网络、Binder IPC 和内核驱动的访问权限。由于 untrusted_app 只能访问少数几个驱动，要利用大多数 OEM 驱动，首先需要进入一个具备相应访问权限的域。
双重静态数据加密（DualDAR，又称 DDAR）是三星 Knox 的一项功能，它在 Android 标准的基于文件的加密（FBE）之上增加了一层独立的加密。这提供了纵深防御：即使外层 FBE 层被攻破，Knox 工作资料中的文件仍受另一套独立密钥体系的保护。
图 1：DualDAR 的数据路径与控制路径。 DualDARComnService 启动 dualdard 并加载其加密库。该守护进程向 /dev/dd 注册，并建立四个共享区域：控制区、元数据区、明文区和密文区。驱动会把每个请求的页面映射到这些区域，供守护进程进行加密或解密。
图 1 展示了 DualDAR 内核驱动与其用户态组件之间的交互。内核驱动将 DualDAR 策略与文件 I/O 集成，并把配置为由用户态执行加密的操作通过 /dev/dd 委托给原生守护进程 dualdard 。对于每个请求，驱动会把数据页和 inode 的元数据页映射到守护进程的地址空间，由守护进程执行所请求的加密或解密。另一个独立的用户态组件 DualDARComnService （Binder 名称： knox_adapter_service ）负责管理这一功能。它运行在 system_server 内，处理启动守护进程、加载其加密库以及将 DualDAR 策略应用到用户数据目录等命令。
对驱动的访问权限决定了漏洞利用链的顺序。在我检查过的设备上，SELinux 拒绝 untrusted_app 访问 /dev/dd 。守护进程以 UID 5250（即 vendor_knoxcore ）运行在 dualdar_app 域中，该域对 knox_dar_device 拥有所需的 chr_file { read write ioctl } 权限。因此，我先利用用户态组件中的一个混淆代理漏洞，在 dualdard 内获得代码执行能力（见阶段 1）。这样就取得了触发内核漏洞所需的访问权限（见阶段 2）。

items.title: [AINews] Math Proofs Are Landing Faster Than We Can Read Them
items.description: November 25, 2026 — From Erdős problems to new bounds for matrix multiplication and Fourier transforms.
items.excerpt:
November 25, 2026 — From Erdős problems to new bounds for matrix multiplication and Fourier transforms. Plus: Thariq at OpenAI!
Scott Aaronson was still trying to digest two proofs of VP ≠ VNP at dinner. Before dessert, an OpenAI paper claimed that the square matrix multiplication exponent ω is exactly 9/4 . During dessert, another paper claimed matching upper and lower bounds for the finite Fourier transform . The lower bound is the biggest news. In October, OpenAI found an upper bound for ω down to at most 9/4 . Finding the lower bound = upper bound leaves only one possible value, which is a shocking result for most.
We plotted 64 selected AI-assisted research advances so far this year. November accounts for 20, including six preprints from Google’s Cogentic . The curve follows public releases, including proofs still under review. We count the two VP ≠ VNP proofs once and give October’s faster matrix multiplication algorithm and November’s matching lower bound an entry each.
The big releases underline how much a paper count can hide. OpenAI’s catalogue lists 730 manuscripts across 375 result families, including follow-ups and companion arguments. Its revision log also records three October withdrawals after a sign error in one paper affected two others. Yupan Liu showed that two messages suffice for quantum interactive proofs , a result that would have been a big deal on its own. Aaronson says Liu used AI and that he had to remind himself the result had even happened.
In other big news, today’s guest Thariq Shihipar announced his big move from Anthropic to OpenAI , the second high profile Ant→OAI move in recent times after Cat Wu . We dive into his two philosophies of AI and how and where /humans add taste.

The investment will help Oversonic expand its manufacturing capacity and bring its robotics solutions to global markets, with a particular focus on the US.

items.excerpt:
A move from California to Portland crosses a state line, a mountain pass and several days of transit. That is enough distance for a small problem to turn into an expensive one, and enough time on the road that you will want to know exactly who is handling your belongings. Before you sign anything, these six checks are worth the effort.
Interstate household goods movers must be registered with the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration, and every legitimate carrier has a USDOT number. A company based in California should also hold a household goods carrier permit from the California Public Utilities Commission, which appears as a CAL-T number.
Ask for both numbers and look them up yourself, starting with the FMCSA’s Protect Your Move resources, rather than taking them on faith. A reputable company hands them over without hesitation.
Some companies run their own trucks and crews. Others sell the job and pass it to a carrier you have not met. Federal guidance expects a legitimate company to say which it is, so ask directly, and ask who will actually load, drive and unload. Either arrangement can work, but you should know which one you are buying.
Federal rules require interstate movers to give written estimates, and the type matters. A binding estimate means you pay no more than the quoted amount at delivery as long as the shipment and services match what was estimated. A non-binding estimate is the mover’s best calculation, and at delivery the mover cannot require more than 110 percent of it. Ask for an in-home or video survey, because a number built from a five-minute phone call is a guess dressed up as a quote.
Plenty of companies will quote a move to Oregon. Fewer run the corridor regularly. A dedicated California to Portland moving company usually has a better feel for realistic transit times, winter conditions near Siskiyou Summit and delivery logistics in Portland’s older neighborhoods and downtown towers, which tends to produce more accurate quotes and fewer surprises on delivery day. Ask how often they run this lane and who will be handling your shipment.
Interstate movers present two levels of liability: full value protection, and a released-value option that pays 60 cents per pound per article. Under the lower option, a ten-pound speaker that arrives broken is worth $6, whatever it cost you. Ask what is included by default, what the higher level involves, how a claim is filed and how long you have to report damage.

items.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
items.excerpt:
Delegating research tasks to AI does not remove scientists’ responsibility for how the work is accomplished. For example, a researcher using AI to review the literature needs to check whether the system overlooks conflicting evidence or makes claims the cited papers don’t support. Someone handing off data analysis to an agentic system needs to understand which methods it used, which files it accessed, and whether the results can be successfully reproduced. A researcher automating part of a lab protocol needs confidence that the system respects physical safety constraints, such as temperature limits or material toxicity, while a researcher working with human-participant data needs assurance that a system protects participants' privacy and limits who can access their information. Researchers also need clear institutional guidelines for verifying and disclosing AI-assisted work.
These ethical and safety questions are central to our work on AI for science. Responsible science is about more than accuracy—scientific fields have ethical research norms because of past actions and choices by scientists and scientific communities, and those norms also cover how research is conducted and what impact it has. We want AI tools to expand what scientists can accomplish without compromising their ability to scrutinize evidence, verify methods, and – perhaps most importantly – stand behind their findings.
To better understand what that requires, we interviewed 17 scientists working in the natural, applied, and social sciences about the responsible development of AI agents. These systems can use tools and carry out research tasks with varying degrees of autonomy. The interviews drew on a network of researchers established through earlier survey work—we wanted to understand how scientists would steer AI’s development to reflect the responsibilities of their fields. We asked where researchers would welcome agentic assistance, what could go wrong, and what safeguards they would need to trust agents with their own studies.
Our interest in these questions grew out of work to evaluate the safety of models developed at Ai2. The OPC Foundation and AutomationML e.V. have announced plans to combine their technologies and communities, with AutomationML becoming part of the OPC Foundation on January 1, 2027.
The agreement will transfer AutomationML’s technology assets to the OPC Foundation, bringing together two organizations that have collaborated for more than a decade on industrial interoperability standards.
The integration aims to establish a more consistent framework for exchanging engineering and operational information across industrial automation systems, supporting digital twins, cloud applications and industrial AI.
AutomationML specializes in exchanging complex engineering information between software tools, engineering disciplines and industrial workflows.
OPC UA provides standardized information models and secure, vendor-independent communication between machines, production systems and enterprise software.
Combining the two technologies is intended to preserve information and its meaning throughout the industrial lifecycle, from engineering and commissioning to production, maintenance and eventual decommissioning.
Dr. Andreas Graf Gatterburg, president of AutomationML, says: “This is the natural next step after more than a decade of collaboration.”
“Together, we can make engineering information a major factor in value creation across the entire industrial lifecycle.”
Stefan Hoppe, president of the OPC Foundation, says: “Industry needs fewer technology silos and more continuity of information.”
“AutomationML strengthens the engineering dimension of the OPC UA ecosystem and helps us move closer to true Plug & Play interoperability.”
The organizations say the integration will help eliminate the traditional separation between engineering information and operational data, allowing industrial systems to retain semantic context across different applications and lifecycle stages.
This could become increasingly important as manufacturers introduce generative and agentic AI into engineering, production and maintenance processes.
The agreement is scheduled to be formally marked at an OPC Foundation press conference during SPS 2026 in Nuremberg, Germany, on November 25.
AutomationML, established in 2009, develops open standards for exchanging engineering information and maintains specifications within the IEC 62714 series.
The OPC Foundation, established in 1996, develops industrial information exchange standards and represents more than 1,010 member organizations worldwide.

items.excerpt:
Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
42 州总检察长介入 Character.AI 的破产程序，试图阻止其拍卖用户私密聊天数据。相关声明称数据集包含超过 2100 万美国账户的聊天记录，其中逾 210 万属于未成年人，还涉及 IP 地址等信息；目前唯一披露的匿名竞拍方为 2026 年 11 月 13 日在特拉华州注册的 Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC，拍卖定于 12 月 1 日。
报道给出涉及 2100 万账户含未成年人的拍卖细节和 42 州总检察长的反对理由，读者可据此了解破产程序下用户数据保护的争议。
当一家 AI公司破产 时，你的私人对话会怎样？如果这家公司是Character.ai，显然他们的计划是把这些对话拍卖给最高出价者。
如今，由42位州总检察长组成的联盟正在介入Character.ai的破产程序，试图阻止这家聊天机器人制造商出售敏感用户数据，其中包含数百万用户的私人对话。
参与此事的各位总检察长分别 发布 了 各自 的 新闻 稿 ，称Character.ai的数据集包含超过2100万个美国账户的聊天记录，其中超过210万个账户属于未成年人。声明还称，此次出售还将涉及IP地址等其他个人数据。
声明还指出，Character.ai已于10月申请第11章破产保护，此前曾向消费者承诺不会出售其个人信息。 （在一篇博客文章中， Character.ai向用户保证，其信息仍将受到隐私政策的保护。）
目前只披露了一个匿名竞标者：Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC（简称Smirks），该公司于2026年11月13日在特拉华州注册成立。据 加州总检察长Rob Bonta指出 ，次日，Character.ai将其选为定于12月1日举行的拍卖的底价。目前尚不清楚买家的聊天记录处置计划。
总检察长们反对此次出售，理由是用户得不到任何保护——他们说，无论谁买下这些数据，都可以为所欲为，包括在不披露的情况下转售数据。买家也不必遵守Character.ai的隐私政策。此外，总检察长们还声称，关于出售后可能出现的任何安全或法律问题，Character.ai向法院提供的信息不如向竞标者提供的信息充分。
此外，包括加州、科罗拉多州、纽约州和康涅狄格州在内的一些州已颁布聊天机器人安全立法，将于2027年1月1日生效，如果此次出售获批，可能会引发更多违规行为。
Bonta在一份 声明 中表示：“Character.AI向消费者承诺不会出售他们的数据。这种行为根据联邦法律和加州法律均属违法，破产不应被用来规避这些消费者保护措施。”
康涅狄格州总检察长William Tong也批评了Character.ai的商业模式。
“他们的聊天机器人把脆弱的青少年推入了情绪波动和性不当对话的兔子洞，”Tong 说 。“他们鲁莽的不当行为和破碎的商业模式把公司拖入了深渊。现在他们想滥用破产程序，去做他们曾承诺不会做的事——把那些私人聊天记录和个人详细信息拍卖给一个来路不明的买家。”
Tong补充道：“我们曾反对迪士尼的出售，现在我们呼吁破产法院也拒绝这笔出售，因为这不过是又一个用来规避法律责任和消费者保护的幌子。”
反对迪士尼这笔交易的一方，是由各州总检察长组成的联盟牵头，成员构成与前者类似但并不完全相同。他们反对的是一项拟议中的2000万美元授权协议，该协议将让 迪士尼获得Character.ai的知识产权 ，但不包括用户的聊天记录。这笔交易尚未获得法院最终批准。（迪士尼还同意 聘用Character.ai剩余的大部分员工 。）
Character.ai的联合创始人诺姆·沙泽尔（Noam Shazeer）和丹尼尔·德弗雷塔斯（Daniel De Freitas） 回归谷歌 后，这家公司便陷入困境——当时这家科技巨头签署了一份非独家授权，获准使用这家人工智能初创公司的技术。该公司还面临与儿童安全相关的诉讼，其中 一起 涉及佛罗里达州一名14岁男孩的自杀，他的母亲称他沉迷于该平台上的一个聊天机器人。

Anthropic 是如何把服务每一个 Claude token 的 API 从 Python 重写成 Rust 的？
今天的嘉宾是 Katelyn Lesse，她负责 Anthropic 的平台工程，此前曾在 Stripe 带领工程团队。她的团队负责 Claude API，以及 Claude Code、Claude Desktop 等产品背后的基础设施。
我们从 Anthropic 从 Python 单体架构转向 Rust 说起。Katelyn 解释了为什么在全球 CPU 短缺的情况下增加 CPU 容量并不容易，Claude 如何帮助工程师快速上手 Rust，以及团队如何用影子流量对照生产流量验证这次重写。 就在今天，Katelyn 和团队发布了 一篇关于他们从 Python 迁移到 Rust 的深度文章。
Katelyn 带我们了解如今 Anthropic 的软件工程工作是什么样子，以及代码审查和值班（oncall）如何与智能体工作流配合。我们还聊到了这家前沿实验室的“软件工厂”、一位产品经理如何把功能上线到生产环境，以及 Anthropic 为什么用基于智能体的练习取代传统的编程面试。
截至上周，Anthropic 已成为上市公司，市值约 1 万亿美元，而员工人数只有其他同等市值公司的十分之一。了解 Anthropic 如何做软件工程，对想要类似结构的公司或许有借鉴意义。
1. Anthropic 用大约五个月时间把 API 从 Python 重写成了 Rust。 这个名为“Messages API”的接口对外承载所有 Claude 的 token 服务，Claude Code 和 Claude Desktop 也走它。该服务负责鉴权、分词、计费和安全性检查，然后调用 GPU 栈生成 token。它原本是一个 Python 单体服务，团队起初对 Python 做了优化，但发现性能开销依然很大，最终决定用 Rust 重写。整个过程由几名工程师参与，前后花了几个月，而且团队里没有人是 Rust 专家！
2. 等等，这个单体服务当初为什么用 Python 写？ 2023 年时，Anthropic 还是一家研究公司，决定要做 API 时，搭建它的团队规模很小，而且很多人同时在做研究。当时研究人员主要用 Python，这让 API 很容易与推理及其他基础设施代码集成。类似地，OpenAI 的 API 最初也是用 Python 写的 ，后来 重写成了 Rust 。Anthropic 和 OpenAI 在 Python 单体服务上遇到了同样的难题：单体服务占用的 CPU 资源逐渐成为越来越大的负担。
3. 这次重写没有 Rust 专家参与，也没有严格的代码审查。 一年前，同一个团队为新服务选了 Go，因为团队成员能读能写这门语言。但到了 2026 年，他们觉得 Claude 的 Rust 水平已经足够好，而 Claude 也在重写过程中帮助工程师进一步了解 Rust。团队没有做严格的代码审查，但拥有一个“不公平”的优势：现有的 Python API 本身就是一套完美的测试基准。他们让新的 Rust API 以影子模式运行在当前 API 旁边，不断迭代，直到所有响应完全一致。此外，Katelyn 估计工程师只仔细看过大约 20% 的生成代码：
“只要你能把某个东西真正拆解到可以用某种方式验证的程度，那就不必逐行去看写出来的每一行 Rust 代码。”
4. Anthropic 有一个全天候运行的代码审查智能体。 公司为所有拉取请求运行了一个 Claude 代码审查分类器，由它来决定：
是否需要人工审查？ 对于“机械性”的低风险改动，比如升级 SDK 版本或改用更新的模型，Claude 可以判定无需人工审查。修复不稳定测试也是如此，这种情况下由另一个 Claude 完成审查，然后合并并部署。

items.excerpt:
Too much AI without a clear pathway to an efficient workflow only adds clutter and confusion, says Deep Current AS.
Dealmaking in logistics technology surged in 2026 and funding is on course to rise, but a softer 2027 freight market will reward only the artificial intelligence (AI) that is embedded in clear workflows and delivers measurable savings, according to a report from Norwegian logistics AI company Deep Current AS.
The report examines developments across freight forwarding, container shipping, warehousing, port operations, logistics services, and supply-chain technology. It draws on conversations with senior executives from logistics, shipping and maritime companies, supported by company disclosures, annual and financial reports, technology investment announcements, and industry research.
"AI has to get smarter in 2027, and smarter means embedded," said Tamim Fannoush, founder and CEO of Deep Current. "The companies that benefit next year will be the ones whose AI sits inside a clear workflow, moves work from one step to the next, and makes it obvious who does what. Too much AI without a clear pathway to an efficient workflow only adds clutter and confusion. Forwarders will keep the tools that make the next step obvious and drop the rest."
For businesses managing physical assets and storage infrastructure, the value of technology extends beyond automation. Reliable data can influence decisions on asset utilisation, inventory management, procurement, pricing, and capacity planning. Digitalisation can improve information sharing across departments, but its value depends on whether the information being shared is consistent and usable.
"The question from forwarders used to be whether AI works. In 2026 it became where AI pays back," Fannoush said. "Investors are funding tools that do operational work, and buyers now want the saving to show up in their numbers."
The market could support brisk investment activity, Deep Current found. Funding to supply chain management and logistics start-ups reached $8.4 billion by mid-August, putting 2026 on course to pass the $9 billion raised in 2025. Deal-making accelerated too, with Capstone Partners counting 66 logistics technology M&A transactions by mid-October, up 73.7% year on year.

Growth is driven by the collection of an increasing number of batteries from electric vehicles, IDTechEx says.
The global market for lithium-ion recycling is set to grow to $64 billion by 2047, driven by the collection of an increasing number of batteries from electric vehicles, according to a report from IDTechEx.
Although lithium-ion battery recycling remains a relatively nascent industry, it is expanding rapidly in response to strategic, economic, and environmental drivers. Already, lithium-ion battery recycling capacity has grown by 77% between 2024 and 2026, and by 2047, over 11 million tonnes of critical battery materials will be available for recovery, the firm said in the report, "Lithium-ion Battery Recycling Market 2027-2047: Markets, Forecasts, Technologies, and Players."
The lithium-ion battery circular economy begins with raw material extraction followed by manufacturing and use, before reaching end-of-life where spent lithium-ion batteries can be recycled to recover these valuable materials. Repurposing, remanufacturing, and recycling all play important roles in reducing waste and improving resource utilization but the latter is the key to closing the loop, enabling the recovery of critical materials that can be reintroduced into the battery supply chain.
Several recycling technologies exist for spent lithium-ion batteries, including mechanical recycling, pyrometallurgical recycling, hydrometallurgical recycling, and direct recycling.
Whatever the method, demand for critical battery materials, such as cobalt, nickel, and lithium is high, so increasing supply through recycling spent lithium-ion batteries is paramount to meeting demand. Virgin production of critical materials will continue but it is limited by geography, so securing production of critical materials from the recycling of lithium-ion batteries means geography is no longer a limiting factor.
The lithium-ion battery recycling industry can expect to be highly profitable, with the market set to grow at 15.3% per year. And returns on investment in recycling facilities are expected to be substantial, with feedstock of spent lithium-ion batteries and manufacturing scrap expected to reach 12.4 million tonnes, so there will be no shortage of material to recycle.

But binding global regulations are required to close the price gap between conventional and renewable fuels, WSC said.
By around 2030, ships already operating or on order that are capable of using renewable marine fuels are expected to account for more than 20% of liner shipping’s total energy demand, demonstrating the scale of potential demand for renewable fuels, according to the World Shipping Council (WSC).
That rising investment in new container ships and vehicle carriers is creating a substantial potential market for renewable marine fuels, WSC said in a report.
However, investment in ships alone will not deliver the energy transition. Without binding global regulations that close the price gap between conventional and renewable fuels, the demand these ships represent risks going unrealised, holding back investment in renewable fuel production and supply infrastructure.
The report found that renewable marine fuels, including both bio-based and synthetic e-fuels, are already being produced and bunkered, although currently on a limited scale. Established fuel industries, renewable electricity resources, and existing infrastructure offer opportunities to expand production in both established bunkering markets and new locations.
"Shipping companies are investing in ships capable of using renewable fuels, and this report shows the opportunities for fuel producers around the world to supply them," said Joe Kramek, President and CEO of World Shipping Council. "The fuels and technologies are already there, but creating a market at scale requires the right commercial conditions. Global regulations that close the price gap with conventional fuels are necessary to unlock investment in production and turn the potential of these ships into real emissions reductions."
Accordingly, WSC is calling for binding global measures with a credible pathway to net zero, consistent enforcement across all ships, and incentives to help close the price gap between conventional and zero- and near-zero GHG fuels.

在 2026 年底用 AI 做开发的人大多已经明白：上下文的质量决定输出的质量。但究竟是什么决定了上下文的质量？
这些来源五花八门，很可能还由不同的人维护，所以你极有可能存在遗留的流程文档，以及过时的事实、指标、决策和策略。
那么，如果你的智能体找到了错误的信息会怎样？或者找到了互相冲突的信息呢？文档 A 说退款政策是 14 天，文档 B 说是 30 天，你的智能体该信哪个？
如果文档有明确的日期，或者智能体读了元数据，它也许能判断出来，但我们想要的可不只是“碰巧事实正确”。
为了寻找解决方案，我开始思考：哪些类型的冲突或问题造成的麻烦最大？我决定做个实验来回答这个问题。
人们常把所有上下文问题都归到 上下文腐化 这个去年出现的说法下，它描述的是会话变得过长、塞满噪音、死胡同和干扰项之后，LLM 的准确率如何下降。
而在真实团队的文件里，情况略有不同。随着几周、几个月过去，你的底层来源（ AGENTS.md 、技能、文档、记忆和代码）会逐渐失去同步，于是智能体可能在一个全新会话的第一轮就拿到互相冲突的指令。这才是真正的 上下文漂移 。
为了把两者放在一起对比测试，我搭了一个逼真的编程沙盒（一个带真实文件和终端工具的 git 仓库），在 Gemini 3.8 Flash 和 Gemini Pro 上跑了 470 个任务，故意植入冗余内容、重复规则、过时文档和直接矛盾。
我原本以为，纯粹由冗余内容造成的上下文腐化会导致明显的错误。结果恰恰相反：注入 5 万个 token 的无关聊天记录，并在多个文件里重复一致的规则，造成的规则违规是 零 ，即使在 Gemini 3.8 Flash 上也是如此。
上下文漂移就完全是另一回事了，而且我是靠阅读模型内部思考过程的摘要（它私下的思维草稿本）才察觉到发生了什么。
在 73% 的运行中，模型在思考时明确注意到两个来源存在分歧。然而在 110 次未加提示的运行中，它向用户提及这一冲突的比例是 0% 。
模型不会警告你，而是悄悄挑一个赢家继续往下走。在 95% 到 100% 的匹配任务中，任务专属的技能文件会覆盖根目录的 AGENTS.md ，即使 AGENTS.md 用了严格的 MUST 措辞也一样。如果你在 AGENTS.md 里更新了一条全仓库规则，却忘了更新某个仍保留旧值的任务专属技能文件，你的智能体几乎每次都会默默遵循那个过时的技能文件。
过时的文档和实际代码对不上时，情况更隐蔽。当文档引用了代码库里早已改名的旧测试辅助函数名，15 次运行中有 9 次会悄悄在新测试文件里写一个单行包装，让 pytest 照样通过，却只字不提这处不一致。
我猜这来自 RLHF 训练。现在的模型被训练得果断、要把活干完，而不是遇到一点小歧义就追着你问，这通常正是智能体工作流用起来顺手的原因。
唯一另一项可测量的代价是斟酌：当两个同级技能文件互相矛盾、又没有明确的裁决依据时，模型会多花 47% 的思考 token 在多个回合里反复争论这处冲突。
我发现模型其实已经在思考轨迹里察觉到了这些冲突，于是试着在 AGENTS.md 里加了一行，让它把分歧在对话里说出来。结果所有完成的运行都做到了（16 次全中）。
不过，我不想让智能体每次写代码都跳出来抱怨文档。所以我把它做成了一个工具：一个只读的小逃生出口，叫 report_inconsistency ，分两类（ conflict 和 stale ）。
（我最初还试过一个 duplicate 类别，但让智能体记录无害的重复内容，会在正常的交叉引用上浪费额外回合，把更多运行推到沙箱 34 回合的上限，尽管仍有 95% 写出了代码，所以我把这个类别砍掉了。）
因为模型在探索时本来就在检查一个文件是否取代另一个文件，调用这个工具几乎不费额外力气。
即便在 AGENTS.md 里 不加任何指令 ，仅仅让这个工具可用，智能体在 Gemini 3.8 Flash 和 Gemini Pro 上就记录了它遇到的 98.7% 的冲突（152 次运行中记录了 150 次），Flash 上零误报。
token 成本也保持不变。在我们的对照测试中，总回合数几乎没动，思考 token 还略有下降（平均约 19%，在正常的运行间波动范围内），所以真正的结论很简单：被动记录基本上是 免费的 。
记录下来的冲突怎么处理由你决定。你可以当场暂停智能体，不过日常工作中我更倾向于让它被动运行：智能体在完成任务的同时记录文件路径、原文引用以及它采用了哪个版本，我之后再查看清理队列。
把一个很小的 MCP 工具接到本地日志文件，就等于给智能体装了一个零额外成本的上下文漂移传感器。在我自己的环境里开启后 24 小时内，它就在一次 PR 审查中抓到了一处真实的规格与代码不一致，而我根本没让它去找。

items.excerpt:
Marine inverters convert the DC power from your battery bank to provide AC power. This means you can have air-conditioning, kitchen appliances and entertainment devices operating on-board without being connected to shore-side power.
To select the correct Marine inverter for your application you must consider several factors. These include the voltage of your battery bank, the AC voltage required and inrush current of your loads. This guide will walk through each consideration, and the power rating and battery bank voltage for each option.
Marine Inverters allow direct current (DC) energy from a battery bank to be converted into alternating current (AC), meaning that you can use standard AC equipment on your vessel. This is useful on vessels that are not located in a marina or place with external power sources.
Air Conditioning, Kitchen Appliances, Refrigeration, Lighting and Entertainment equipment can be powered using Marine Inverters. Pumps, computers, instrumentation and communications can also be powered from Marine Inverters. The equipment that can be powered depends on the power of the inverter and energy available in the battery bank.
Marine Inverters do not produce energy, nor charge the battery bank. The inverter simply converts the energy in the battery from DC to AC. The battery can be charged from an engine, generator, solar and external power sources, depending on the set-up of electrical systems on the vessel.
Therefore, it is important to choose a Marine Inverter of suitable specification based on the battery bank, loads and applications on your vessel.
Many vessels cannot connect to mains electricity. Without suitable electrical equipment on board, it can be difficult to use standard AC equipment. Marine Inverters allow energy from the vessel’s battery bank to be converted to AC to allow this equipment to be used.
On pleasure vessels, this may be kitchen appliances, air conditioning, cooling systems and entertainment. On commercial vessels, pumps, refrigeration, computers and communication equipment may need AC power. Choosing a Marine Inverter of suitable size means that these loads can be powered on vessels in locations away from land.
Consideration must be given to the total electrical system. Based on the battery size, and inverter size, you will be able to know how much energy can be supplied in AC form. This is important in creating a reliable electrical system on board.
The type of AC produced by the marine inverter can be important.

items.title: Inventory-Light Retail Is an Order-Orchestration Problem
items.description: Inventory-light retail requires coordinated, cost-aware order promises across inventory, order management, WMS, transportation, and exception handling. The post Inventory-Light Retail Is an Order-Orchestration Problem appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A customer examines a sample sofa in a showroom and asks a straightforward question: Can you deliver it on Friday?
The salesperson sees three units available in the order system and answers yes. Two days later, the customer receives a call. One unit was damaged, another is already reserved, and the third is in a warehouse that cannot arrange a two-person delivery crew until Tuesday.
This is the point where a retail concept becomes a logistics systems problem. The store delivered a good selling experience. The network could not deliver the promise.
When inventory and the customer-facing transaction are separated, the quality of the experience depends on coordination across order management, inventory, warehouse execution, and transportation. Those systems often exist already. The difficulty is getting them to make one coherent decision before the retailer commits to the customer.
An inventory-light format demands more than visibility. It demands executable promises.
An inventory screen can show three units on hand. That tells us very little about whether one can be delivered by Friday.
One may be committed to another order. Another may be damaged or awaiting inspection. The remaining unit may be in a facility with a full pick schedule or a missed outbound cutoff. Even physically available inventory can be operationally unavailable for the desired service window.
A reliable promise requires a sequence of checks. Is there a valid sellable unit? Can it be reserved without conflict? Is the item in a location that can release it in time? Can the transport network reach the delivery address at the required service level? Does the order require installation, a specific vehicle, or a scheduled crew?
This is the difference between basic available-to-promise logic and a more comprehensive capacity-aware commitment. It is particularly important for furniture, appliances, and orders with complex installation requirements. The customer does not care which subsystem caused the delay. The customer remembers that the date promised in the store was wrong.
The same issue applies to the retailer using stores as fulfillment nodes. Target’s 2025 annual report says stores fulfilled 97.6 percent of merchandise sales, including store purchases and digitally originated orders fulfilled from stores. items.title: How Reliable Network Infrastructure is Shaping the Future of Industrial Automation
items.description: A robot cell stops mid-task, yet the maintenance crew finds nothing wrong with its mechanics. items.excerpt:
A robot cell stops mid-task, yet the maintenance crew finds nothing wrong with its mechanics. The interruption traces back to a delayed network message, leaving engineers investigating a connection rather than a motor.
Industrial automation now extends beyond fenced factory cells into mines, energy sites, warehouses, and moving fleets. Each additional camera, robot, and sensor adds traffic that must arrive in time for the equipment using it.
Reliable network infrastructure consequently belongs in the same engineering conversation as machine performance. That changes what reliability must mean for machines, rather than office users waiting for a file to download.
For automation, reliability involves timing, available capacity, and traffic separation. Each needs its own acceptance test before equipment enters production.
Latency, the delay before information arrives, matters differently from download speed. Jitter, variation in that delay, complicates control loops: the repeated exchanges between sensors and controllers that guide a machine. A connection with impressive average throughput can still deliver individual commands too late.
Machine vision, remote operation, and video feeds also need predictable delivery, although their timing requirements differ. A delayed command can interrupt a robot cell; a mobile vehicle should slow or pause safely when its connection degrades. Engineers therefore need to evaluate performance during busy periods, with cameras streaming and production systems exchanging data, rather than accepting an unloaded speed test at commissioning.
Fiber inside a factory does not solve connectivity for a pipeline, construction camp, or moving fleet. Mines and energy installations also need connections where terrestrial coverage is unavailable, with capacity allocated to operational traffic before routine downloads.
At remote sites, a consumer plan shares capacity without promising a particular busy-hour speed. One provider lists enterprise-grade satellite service with a committed information rate (CIR), a minimum bandwidth guaranteed to the site. That distinction matters for supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA), which gathers measurements and supports remote supervision. Capacity planning should account for routine polling, alarm messages, and remote monitoring, rather than sizing the connection around occasional file transfers alone.

items.title: An Indic Voice Agent with CUGA
items.excerpt:
Most useful knowledge is written and digitized in English. Most of the people who need it speak, and think, in their own regional languages like Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, Marathi and many others. Many would rather talk than type.
We built a small voice agent to close that gap, using CUGA as the agent harness. This post explains the use case and what we learned. You can try it yourself in CUGA Apps .
A farmer asks a question aloud, in their own language: how do I tell good seed from bad? The agent:
If someone asks about cricket or coding, it politely steers them back to farming instead of making something up.
CUGA (ConfigUrable Generalist Agent) is IBM Research's open-source agent harness. It handles the model wiring, tool management, state and guardrails, so you write tools and a prompt instead of the agent loop. Here we use it as an embedded SDK inside a small web app, for three things:
The key design idea is simple: CUGA is a text-in, text-out brain. Voice is two thin layers around it.
Because the agent only ever sees text, you can build and test it with plain text first, then add the ears and the mouth. You can also swap speech providers without touching the agent. We support two: Sarvam AI's cloud speech APIs, called directly from the user's browser, and open-source models (SraVaani for speech-to-text, Svara for text-to-speech) running on your own server.
Adding speech is the easy part. The hard part is cross-lingual retrieval : a Hindi question has to find an English paragraph.
Search works by turning text into vectors and finding the nearest ones. CUGA's default embedding model is English-only, so it turns Hindi into vectors that carry almost no meaning. With it, a Hindi or Tamil question still retrieves five passages, but they are the wrong ones. The model, correctly told to answer only from what it was given, quietly says "the handbook doesn't cover that". Every layer behaves correctly, so there is no error and no warning.
The fix is to use a multilingual embedding model (we use intfloat/multilingual-e5-large ), so the same meaning lands in the same place whatever the language. Conceptually simple, though wiring it into CUGA took a small workaround (shown in the tutorial). After that, one English document serves every language, and you do not need translated copies of anything.

items.title: Researcher develops quantum-inspired approach to safer autonomous drone navigation
items.description: US-based independent researcher Dr Sai Krishna Thota has developed a quantum-inspired decision-support framework designed to improve the safety and reliability of autonomous drone navigation by prioritizing operational risks alongside conventional route planning objectives. The research, published in Elsevier’s journal Knowledge-Based Systems, addresses the limitations of conventional navigation methods that prioritize finding the shortest route between […]
items.excerpt:
US-based independent researcher Dr Sai Krishna Thota has developed a quantum-inspired decision-support framework designed to improve the safety and reliability of autonomous drone navigation by prioritizing operational risks alongside conventional route planning objectives.
The research, published in Elsevier’s journal Knowledge-Based Systems , addresses the limitations of conventional navigation methods that prioritize finding the shortest route between two locations.
Autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly being used in applications including infrastructure inspection, emergency response, logistics and environmental monitoring, where operating conditions can present significant challenges.
The proposed framework takes into account factors including energy consumption, communication reliability, weather conditions and safety requirements when evaluating potential routes.
Across 180 simulated mission scenarios, the framework reduced average route risk by approximately 20.5 percent and safety-rule violations by 52.8 percent compared with an existing risk-aware planning method.
However, the research also identified a trade-off between improved safety and increased energy consumption.
Thota, a senior member of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), says: “The research introduces a knowledge-guided, quantum-inspired framework that helps autonomous drones prioritize safety over simply finding the shortest route.”
Although the framework draws on mathematical concepts associated with quantum computing, it operates using conventional computing technology and does not require quantum hardware.
The study also found that incorporating explicit operational rules contributed more significantly to improvements in overall performance than the quantum-inspired component.
The findings highlight the potential of knowledge-based decision-support systems to improve the reliability and explainability of autonomous navigation.
While the results are based on computer simulations rather than physical drone trials, the research could inform further investigations into safer autonomous aerial operations.

UK robotics software startup Path2 is developing a browser-based robot cell design and programming platform aimed at helping smaller manufacturers automate production processes without the need for substantial systems integration budgets.
Founded by Sam Reynolds, a chartered engineer and certified machinery safety expert, Path2 enables users to design robotic workcells by positioning robots, conveyors, pallets and safety guarding within a virtual environment.
Users can teach robot positions on screen, check whether the robot can reach the required locations and generate robot programs without manually writing code.
In a demonstration using a Kuka KR 210 R2700 extra industrial robot, Reynolds went from a blank cell layout to a running palletizing cycle in 19 minutes.
Reynolds says: “On a real Kuka KR 210 R2700 extra it went from blank layout to a running cycle in 19 minutes, with no KRL written, no positions taught on the pendant and no edits.”
The platform currently supports 20 Kuka robot models with payload capacities ranging from 20 to 800 kg. Support for ABB, Fanuc, Universal Robots and other major robot manufacturers is planned.
Path2 is also developing a comprehensive downloadable engineering package that will include robot programs, dimensioned layouts, component drawings, parts lists, electrical documentation and commissioning checklists.
Future capabilities will guide users through machinery safety processes, including risk assessments, safety requirements, performance levels and CE marking.
The browser-based cell design tools are available free of charge, with commercial downloads scheduled to become available shortly.
Path2 plans to charge £495 for an individual robot cell design package, while a subscription costing £99 per month will provide access to unlimited cell design packages.
The company is also recruiting beta testers to evaluate its software using physical robots or simulation environments.

Testing and certification company TÜV SÜD has awarded its Human-Machine Performance Certification to wearable robotics specialist Ascentiz , covering its Pro and Ultra modular hip exoskeletons.
The certification follows independent testing across key performance indicators, including physical workload reduction, fatigue relief, operating range and noise levels.
Working with CAICT CTTL, TÜV SÜD evaluated the exoskeletons across seven everyday activities: walking, running, ascending and descending stairs, walking uphill, cycling and squatting.
During uphill walking, exertion in key muscle groups decreased by more than 44 percent. Maximum reductions in participants’ metabolic expenditure ranged from 16.71 to 44.87 percent across several activities.
Operating range tests demonstrated that the exoskeleton could travel more than 6 km under demanding conditions involving maximum assistance and an incline. Under normal operating conditions, its theoretical range exceeds 25 km.
The device delivered peak hip extension torque of approximately 22.5 Nm per side, with a difference in assistance output between the two sides of less than 1 percent.
Cody Kou, vice president of international business at Ascentiz Innovation, says: “We are honoured to receive the Human-Machine Performance Certification from TÜV SÜD. It recognizes our commitment to putting users’ real-world experience at the centre of product development.
“Through modular design, we aim to make exoskeleton technology accessible in an increasingly broad range of everyday applications.”
Radu Gosav, vice president of EMC and RF services at TÜV SÜD North Asia, says: “As exoskeletons interact directly with the human body, their performance needs to be evaluated from both technical and human perspectives.
“Our Human-Machine Performance Certification provides an independent assessment of how effectively these devices support users in real-world activities.
“We will continue to contribute our testing expertise to the standardized development of the consumer exoskeleton industry.”

Bentic – an Emerald Technology Ventures portfolio company – is advancing the commercial use of physical AI in industrial automation, with nearly 100 robots deployed at customer production sites.
The Munich-based company is preparing to enter the US market with technology that enables robots to handle deformable materials such as textiles, cables, carbon fiber and food. These are tasks that have traditionally required human dexterity and have resisted conventional automation.
Formerly known as sewts, bentic addresses a longstanding limitation in industrial robotics: the difficulty of reliably handling materials that change shape, move unpredictably or lack a consistent structure.
The company’s approach relies on training AI with real-world industrial data. Rather than depending primarily on laboratory testing and simulation, its systems learn from actual production environments, using operational experience to improve their ability to recognize and manipulate materials under changing conditions. Emerald led bentic’s €7 million Series A financing in August 2023, backing its approach to making industrial automation more adaptable.
Mehran Zaker, partner and head of industrial AI and robotics, Emerald Technology Ventures, says: “For decades, industrial robots have been limited by the assumption that the world around them must be predictable. Physical AI is changing that equation.
“bentic is showing that robots can learn to work with the complexity of the real world, handling materials and performing tasks that have long resisted automation. This is no longer a theoretical possibility. It’s already happening on factory floors.”
bentic’s technology combines two core capabilities: a foundational intelligence that predicts how deformable materials behave and an action model that translates those predictions into robot movements. Together, they enable robots to manipulate materials that conventional automation struggles to handle consistently.
Applications include textile processing, e-commerce returns, automotive cable harnesses, technical textiles, carbon fiber components and food processing.
The company’s robot-agnostic platform, Jupiter, allows individual robots to benefit from operational experience gathered across the installed fleet. This growing body of real-world training data can improve performance across different materials and applications.

In a new article, Why Reliability Will Define the Next Decade of Robotics, HBK examines the importance of reliability engineering across applications ranging from humanoid robots and warehouse automation to robotic surgery and subsea inspection.

For humanoid robots, the challenge is particularly complex. Actuators, sensors, controllers, joints and structural components must work together in environments that are often unpredictable. A failure in one subsystem can compromise the performance of the entire machine.
Some humanoid robotics developers are incorporating Design for Reliability (DfR) methodologies into their development processes, using engineering software such as HBK’s ReliaSoft to assess potential weaknesses at both component and system levels.

HBK says one major warehouse automation company is using its software to analyze reliability, availability and maintainability across a large robotic fleet.
Similar considerations apply to medical robotics, where reliability is closely linked to precision, patient safety and regulatory compliance.
HBK says a global medical technology company developing robotic surgical systems is using its software to analyze component lifespans and identify potential risks during development.
Meanwhile, a developer of advanced seabed imaging technology is using reliability modeling to understand how individual equipment failures could affect entire missions in environments where maintenance is particularly difficult and costly.

Neuryn Robotics , a Madrid-based startup developing AI-powered robotic systems for processing fashion e-commerce returns, was among 20 finalists at Alibaba.com’s CoCreate Pitch London 2026 competition.
The Spanish company presented its technology on November 20 at ExCeL London to a judging panel that included former professional footballer Rio Ferdinand, entrepreneur Deborah Meaden, Simon Squibb, Tijen Onaran and Jonathan Anguelov.
Although Neuryn Robotics did not finish among the top three, the company says it is due to receive a $10,000 award as one of the competition’s finalists.
Neuryn Robotics is developing robotic systems designed to automate several stages of the returns handling process, from unpacking garments to inspecting their condition and determining their next destination.
The robots use artificial intelligence to assess individual items of clothing and decide whether they are suitable for resale or should be sent for repair or recycling.
Processing returned clothing presents a particular challenge for automation because garments vary considerably in size, shape, material and condition, making them more difficult to handle than rigid, uniformly packaged products.
The technology could also help retailers address growing regulatory and environmental pressures associated with the management of returned and unsold merchandise.
In July 2026, a European Union ban on the destruction of unsold apparel and footwear came into effect for large companies, increasing the importance of alternative approaches to managing surplus inventory.
Neuryn Robotics is entering a market in which other robotics companies are already working with major fashion retailers.
German robotics company Sereact, for example, has been working with European online fashion retailer Zalando to automate returns processing using AI-powered robotic systems.

items.excerpt:
A practical guide to shipping with Claude Code
Anthropic Claude Code 团队刚推出 Claude Ship，包含三个智能体：Code Review（已全面开放）、PR Steward 和 Claude Approvals（beta），可审查 PR、处理失败 CI、合并冲突和审查意见，并按仓库策略文件批准常规改动。
Claude Code 团队成员亲自梳理了 PR 后续流程的三个智能体分工和落地步骤，开发者可按需迁移到自己的仓库。
我们刚刚推出了 Claude Ship ，它可以审查你的拉取请求、着手修复，并在团队策略允许的情况下批准这些请求。你或许已经有一套自定义技能或工作流来完成这些步骤，但我们想提供另一种选择。本指南基于我在 Claude Code 团队的经验，逐步介绍这套流程。
在我们团队，这类后续工作通常由智能体来完成。比如，它可以接手审查者发现的问题，这样作者回来时，PR 已经更新过一轮了。
以我的经验，这是一种更高效、也更愉快的编码方式。它减少了上下文切换，让我保持心流状态。
我们 这里 讲过 Claude Code 团队的代码审查流程，也 这里 讲过其底层的验证流程。
Claude Ship 面向的是团队使用 GitHub、且没有管理员权限的开发者或技术负责人。你现在就可以自己动手，运行几条命令开始，并把学到的东西保存到仓库文件里供团队审阅。只有当你希望智能体自动处理团队的 PR 时，才需要管理员介入。
Claude Ship 由三个智能体来承担这项工作：Code Review、PR Steward（测试版）和 Claude Approvals（测试版）。
Code Review 会从多个视角对照代码库对拉取请求做深入审查。它收集发现的问题，以对抗性方式加以验证，分类后发布到 PR 上。
PR Steward 负责让 PR 保持绿灯，但它的设计目标不是批准或合并拉取请求。它会在 CI 检查失败、出现合并冲突，以及收到 Code Review、其他审查工具或团队成员的审查反馈时介入。每次推送后，它都会评论说明改了什么、如何撤销。
在此基础上， Claude Approvals 会应用一套由团队写成仓库文件的批准策略。如果策略允许，Claude 可以自行批准常规改动；某些场景下，也可以要求更深入的人工签核。它就像一个更聪明的 CODEOWNERS 文件。团队可以让 Claude Approvals 在决策时参考多种信号，包括 Code Review 的发现或团队自己的分类器。
Code Review 已正式可用，另外两个处于测试阶段。/ship 是你在 Claude Code 中自行运行的命令，用来对自己的拉取请求试用 Claude Ship。它随最新版 Claude Code 提供，即使管理员尚未开启任何智能体也能使用。
前两步今天就可以部分自动化。最后一步是一个决定，由你在分支保护设置和（如果团队采用了的话）策略文件中设定。下面按 Claude Ship 包含的三个智能体来拆解：
如果这篇帖子你只做一件事，那就是在推送前先审查自己的分支。此时发现的 bug，之后就不太可能变成评审意见或失败的检查项，把你从下一个任务上拽回来。在 Claude Code 提示符下输入这条命令：
它会审查你分支上的提交以及尚未提交的改动，找出正确性方面的 bug。有几种变体需要留意：
effort 范围从 low 到 max，low 只返回审查最有把握的发现，级别越高给出的结果越宽泛（包括一些把握不大的）。命令会记住你上次用的 effort，所以风险等级变了就重新输入一个。
你首先要做的是多跑几次 /code-review，弄清它能抓到什么、在哪些地方会出错。后面你会用到这些经验。
第一步里 /ship 会像运行了 git add -A 一样提交你待处理的改动，这一点有时会让人措手不及，所以运行 /ship 前务必先跑一下 git status。
该命令不会提交涉及文件名看起来像密钥的改动，也不会提交设置规则的文件，比如 CLAUDE.md、REVIEW.md，以及 .claude/ 或 .github/ 目录下的任何内容。这些需要你事先手动提交。
另外，如果你在公开仓库中工作，该命令不会替你提交任何改动。你需要先手动提交所有待处理的改动才能继续；如果 PR 已经存在，它也不会包含你待处理的改动。
默认情况下，该命令会读取你本人、有写权限的人以及 Claude GitHub App 的评论。你可以用 +name 的形式指定额外的机器人。如果该机器人发表了评论，它会被当作一条断言，对照代码进行检查。
Claude 以你的身份、在你的机器上关注 PR，并消耗你的配额。合上笔记本电脑它就会停止，所以要保持会话打开、机器不休眠。你还需要登录 GitHub CLI（先运行 gh auth login），而且它只关注你打开的 PR。
除了 自动模式 之外， watch 会在每个提示处停下，等待你回应。它不会在 bypass-permissions 模式下运行。注意在 Windows 上，/ship 会打开 PR 并进行审查，但 watch 不会启动。

Autonomous drone delivery company Zipline and restaurant chain Chipotle have completed what the companies describe as the first drone food delivery in PGA Tour history, delivering freshly prepared meals to two professional golfers during a practice round in Austin, Texas.
The delivery took place on the 18th hole of the Fazio Canyons course at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa, where Joel Dahmen and Mark Hubbard were preparing for the Austin Championship.
Video footage of the delivery shows the drone lowering a package directly onto the golf course.
Dahmen ordered a steak bowl with chips and Queso Blanco, while Hubbard opted for a steak burrito with guacamole.
Dahmen says: “Usually after a round, we’re the ones making a Chipotle run. This time, Chipotle came to us.
“When your burrito can meet you on 18, it makes you rethink what’s possible.”
Chipotle first partnered with Zipline in 2025 to expand its delivery capabilities beyond conventional destinations, including backyards and public parks.
The drone food delivery service is currently available to Chipotle customers in Dallas and Austin, Texas.
Arlie Sisson, chief digital officer at Chipotle, says: “A golf course isn’t a place you’d traditionally expect to have a freshly prepared meal delivered—or, even better, have it arrive from the sky. That’s what makes this moment so exciting.
“Together with Zipline, we’re using technology to redefine convenience and bring Chipotle to our guests.”
Although the golf course delivery was a promotional initiative, it illustrates the potential for autonomous aerial delivery systems to serve locations that are not easily accessible through conventional road-based delivery services.

items.excerpt:
MIT 和 Microsoft 的新论文《AI-Assisted Programming and Labor Demand》利用 5,414 家跨国公司（覆盖 38% 美国程序员）的 GitHub 合同审查时点构造自然实验，估计 Copilot 采用对劳动力需求的影响。
论文用合同审查时点构造自然实验，给出了 Copilot 采用对初级工程师招聘影响的因果证据，可作讨论 AI 与就业的依据。
总体而言，该论文发现GitHub Copilot减少了大公司对初级程序员的招聘，而员工离职和高级人员招聘则保持平稳。
早期采用AI的公司在招聘和增长方式上已经有所不同，因此简单的比较无法显示AI编程工具对就业的影响。此前关于这一问题的研究得出了相互矛盾的答案。
他们追踪了5,414家跨国公司，覆盖了38%的美国程序员，这些公司的GitHub合同审查时间设定在Copilot发布之前。审查时间较早的公司更早采用了Copilot，这形成了一个自然实验。
1年后，在被审查日期推动采用Copilot的公司中，季度技术招聘下降了29%，而离职率没有上升。其初级软件工程师招聘下降了约40%，而有经验的工程师招聘保持稳定。
在Copilot之前，72%的初级技术招聘进入了编码密集型岗位。采用之后这一比例为52%，因此入门级招聘最终在编码密集型和非编码密集型岗位之间大致平均分配。

items.title: Consumer Confidence Surged in November
items.description: One cause of the confidence was due to lower uncertainty following the midterm elections, said Fergus McCormick, of The Conference Board.
items.excerpt:
Just in time for the holiday season, consumer confidence has increased.
The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index rose by 11.4 points to 103.3 (1985=100) in November, up from 91.9 in October.
“Consumer confidence rallied again in November, potentially due to lower uncertainty following the midterm elections,” said Fergus McCormick, senior economist, Global Indicators, The Conference Board , in a statement.
“After two months of consecutive increases, the headline index is back to levels of confidence last seen in January 2025. The gain in confidence was led by stronger perceptions of present and future labor market conditions. Perceptions of current and future business conditions also improved sharply. Along with the gain in headline confidence, consumers planned slightly higher spending on goods and vacations.”
All age groups and generations recorded an increase in confidence in November, with the greatest increase by Gen Z respondents. Improvements in confidence were largest among consumers with higher household incomes.
McCormick continued: “Write-in responses in November were slightly less negative than previous months. While consumers continued to express frustration with high prices and rising costs, some comments cited hope for the general economy. Comments about war and conflict ticked up slightly, along with mixed feelings about elections, politics, and the direction of the labor market.”
On a month-over-month as well as on a six-month moving average basis, plans to purchase autos and homes both improved slightly in November.
Planned spending on durable goods in the month generally increased across the board.
Expected spending on services over the next six months was mixed. Anticipated spending on hotels and airfare for personal travel increased.
Other increases in planned spending remained concentrated on discretionary items such as gambling and lottery, amusement parks and/or outdoor recreation, and historic sites, museums, and libraries. The top spending plans included restaurants, bars, take-out; streaming, internet, mobile services; utilities; health care; and beauty, personal care, but these categories were somewhat less prioritized compared to previous months.

Three months ago, shortly after the Demis/Dean/etc departures , and with disappointing progress on Gemini 3 models, people had publicly given up on Google DeepMind as a frontier lab. Today, apologies are being issued , and Neon is the talk of the town!
Despite giving Gemini 4 Argon (RIP), Carbon and Neon the title story (with Hydrogen a near miss ), we are exercising yet another rare double-feature choice to highlight the unusually strong breakout trend in Neon’s adoption:
If this seems like a coordinated hype campaign, it very probably isn’t, mostly because the names we feature can’t be bought, especially coming up to the end.
AI News for 11/23/2026-11/24/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies!
Frontier Models as Research Engines: VP ≠ VNP, Protein Design and 948 Kernel Bugs
VP ≠ VNP, posted by two labs : An Anthropic GitHub repo reportedly contains a proof by an internal Claude research model that VP ≠ VNP. This is the algebraic analogue of P vs NP, posed by Valiant in 1979, and implies that polynomials such as the permanent lack small circuits over every field ( @kimmonismus , repo pointer ).
OpenAI's counter-release : OpenAI then posted its own proof and says it was "obtained on November 6, 2026." Neither lab named a model or published an announcement ( @AndrewCurran_ ).
Scope : The result does not imply P ≠ NP, which still requires general Boolean circuit lower bounds ( @ZhihuFrontier ).
Speculation : Curran argues that both labs are sitting on unreleased results and repeats unconfirmed rumors of cryptography breakthroughs. Treat this as opinion.
Riemann proof clarifications : Levent Alpöge says the "250,000+ pages" claim was a joke. He released only the Lean code because he could not produce a readable writeup, and called it "full of garbage obviously, but compiles" ( @kimmonismus , @simonw ).
Lineage claim : A Zhihu analysis traces Alpöge's key method to a short OpenAI proof excluding Landau–Siegel zeros. This is an attributed inference ( @ZhihuFrontier ).
GPT-6 protein design, wet-lab validated : OpenAI released a preprint showing GPT-6 models designing new protein shapes and sequences through reasoning and code, without specialized bio models ( @OpenAI ).

IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，彭博社昨日（11 月 24 日）发布博文，报道称“人类史上最大 IPO”上市（11 月 19 日）的 Anthropic 首次跌破每股 83 美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 554.3 元人民币） 的 IPO 发行价， 美国东部时间 11 月 24 日 16 点（北京时间 25 日凌晨 4 点）收报 81.91 美元 （现汇率约合 547 元人民币） ，单日下跌 6.54%。
这家上周刚创下纪录登陆纳斯达克的 AI 公司，上市首日曾以 111.50 美元 （现汇率约合 744.6 元人民币） 开盘，较发行价高出 34%，盘中一度突破 115 美元 （现汇率约合 768 元人民币） ，完全稀释估值一度超过 2 万亿美元 （现汇率约合 13.36 万亿元人民币） 。
然而，短短数个交易日后，市场情绪迅速逆转。Anthropic 盘中最低跌至约 76 美元 （现汇率约合 507.5 元人民币） ，较发行价低近 9%，较上市首日高点回撤约 34%；路透社测算，其市值一度面临蒸发近 2,000 亿美元 （现汇率约合 1.34 万亿元人民币） 的压力。
本轮下跌并非 Anthropic 独有。市场对 AI 企业盈利能力、巨额算力资本开支以及高估值可持续性的疑虑升温，引发科技股广泛抛售。上周，标普 500 指数与道琼斯工业指数双双进入技术性回调区间，英伟达则录得 2008 年以来最大单周跌幅。
值得注意的是，尽管英伟达在黄仁勋恢复 CEO 职务后带动 AI 相关股票一度反弹，Anthropic 仍未能跟随上涨，彭博社认为投资者正更严格审视 AI 公司的基本面与现金流。

作为10月6日发布的一部分，我们在矩阵乘法指数上取得了一个特别干净的进展，得到了9/4的新上界。自那以后，模型一直在研究这个指数的下界。这已经相当疯狂了，因为关于下界此前一无所知！今天我们宣布，实际上9/4是紧的……这真的是那种我从没想过这辈子能见到的结果。

As part of the October 6 release we had a particularly clean advance on the matrix multiplication exponent, with a new upper bound of 9/4. Since then, the model has been working on a LOWER BOUND for this exponent. This is already pretty crazy since NOTHING was known for lower bounds! Today we announced that actually 9/4 is tight ... This is really the kind of result that I never thought I would see in my lifetime.
(btw, by an "old" result of Yin Tat Lee and collaborators this also implies that linear programs can be solved in time n^{9/4}.)

items.title: Hill-climbing Inkling 2 Mini inference on one RTX PRO 6000
items.excerpt:
Inkling 2 Mini came out last week and sets a new state of the art for local AI and smaller open-source models. With ~26B total parameters (3B active per token), multimodal inputs, and a 1M-token context window, it leads its weight class on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 and across 32 of 48 benchmarks against models like Gemma 4 31B and Qwen3.8-27B, making it a strong open option for coding, tool use, and reasoning on modest hardware. We wrote an extensive blog post on how you can use it within the Hugging Face ecosystem here .
One of the interesting aspects of Inkling 2 Mini that might explain its great performance is its unusual architecture. Inkling 2 Mini is a looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 24 physical layers where the middle 12 layers run three times, so every token passes through 48 layers. The checkpoint ships in mixed NVFP4 and MXFP8 and bundles a DSpark drafter for speculative decoding. Both vLLM and SGLang, the go-to frameworks for LLM inference, support it on nightly builds, though the published serving recipes target NVIDIA B200 and GB300 GPUs ( sm100 ), leaving out sm120 cards like the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 where kernel compatibility can differ.
We wanted to see how fast we could serve it on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 96 GB, the GPU behind an nvidia-rtx-pro-6000 Inference Endpoint . Rather than tuning flags by hand, we gave a coding agent the inference-optimisation skill, the hf CLI, and access to Hugging Face Jobs , and let it run experiments for an afternoon.
Across 46 valid benchmark runs, single-user decode went from 136 to 190.6 tok/s (+40%) (ahead of the 167.7 tok/s community SGLang + DSpark benchmark on LocalMaxxing for the same GPU) and 8-user aggregate throughput went from ~570 to 716 tok/s (+26%) using vLLM nightly with DSpark speculative decoding. Greedy outputs are byte-identical with and without speculation, long-context needle retrieval passes 3/3 up to 250K tokens, and the winning config is now running as an Inference Endpoint from a pinned image digest. All logs, scripts, and raw measurements are in NielsRogge/inkling-2-mini-hillclimb .
The inference-optimisation skill gives an agent a fixed experimental protocol and a small, engine-agnostic benchmark script ( bench.py ):

I gave a keynote at the AI Engineer Code Summit a couple of weeks ago, constructed around the idea that there have been three significant inflection points in the abilities of LLMs and coding agents in the past twelve months.
Here’s the video of the talk. In this post I’m going to pull out the major inflection point theme and interrogate it more deeply.
Today, November 24th 2026, is the one year anniversary of the release of Claude Opus 4.5 . With hindsight, this was a consequential model.
In the Opus 4.5 announcement, Anthropic said:
Testers noted that Claude Opus 4.5 handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding. They told us that, when pointed at a complex, multi-system bug, Opus 4.5 figures out the fix. They said that tasks that were near-impossible for Sonnet 4.5 just a few weeks ago are now within reach.
Claude Code was 9 months old at that point, having been introduced alongside Claude 3.7 Sonnet on February 24th, 2025.
Opus 4.5 was the first model I had used with Claude Code where the default result was generally the right thing. I hadn’t been using Claude Code as a daily driver because it didn’t feel reliable enough—I had to correct it often enough that it didn’t feel like a clear accelerant.
The new Opus changed that. For most of the coding problems I faced on a daily basis, Opus would get them right . It was clearly faster than working through the problems myself.
Also in November, OpenAI released GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, GPT-5.1-Codex, and GPT-5.1-Codex-Max. These had a similar effect on their Codex coding agent: it became reliably useful for many of my coding tasks.
The timing was convenient, because the December holidays were upon us. A lot of people, myself included, spent December tinkering with these new tools to see what they could do. By January we were ready to use them for our actual work.
We got our first hint of Claude Fable in April, when Anthropic announced Claude Mythos and said that it was too dangerous to release , due to its improved cybersecurity capabilities. Mythos was a model that could not just find security vulnerabilities, it could also figure out how to exploit them.
In June we got to see how good that model was for ourselves, with the release of Claude Fable 5—a defanged Mythos, that would solve most problems but would actively block you from using it for security work.

As freight theft rates continue to rise, the supply chain risk analysis firm Verisk CargoNet is recommending that shippers, brokers, and carriers tighten their security and verification processes from Tuesday, Nov. 24, through Monday, Nov. 30.
The firm is highlighting a growing scheme in which cybercriminals posing as drivers and dispatchers respond to carriers' job postings on social media, gain access to company email and phone systems, and use those systems to bid on and steal shipments in the carrier's name.
Verisk CargoNet said its concern in 2026 is not only what is being stolen, but how criminals are gaining access to freight. Cybercriminals are operating under the identities of legitimate carriers, and a growing number are able to execute thefts through standard carrier practices.
Among the schemes of greatest concern to Verisk CargoNet this season are highly technical tactics in which criminals operate under the identity of a legitimate carrier. They compromise a carrier's email account, deceive a carrier already hauling a shipment into delivering it elsewhere, or buy an existing carrier’s credentials.
"The groups behind these schemes are patient, and they plan around the calendar," said Keith Lewis, vice president of operations, Verisk CargoNet. "A carrier's email address and phone number are how brokers know who they are dealing with. Guard access to them the way you guard the keys to your trucks."

More specifically, cargo thieves in 2026 continue to favor full-truckload shipments of metals and the enterprise computing hardware used in data centers. Thieves also target components such as fiber optic transceivers, central processors, graphics processors and memory chips.

As hyperscalers buy large volumes of servers, racks, components, and spare parts, they need additional material handling equipment and warehouse automation, Interact Analysis says.
Rapid growth in data center construction is creating demand for material handling equipment and warehouse automation to manage the rising volumes of technology components like servers, racks, components, and spare parts, according to a report by Interact Analysis.
The rising demand for logistics services occurs because all the technical hardware that powers data center operations must be stored, staged, integrated, and moved.
Of the different types of facilities in the data center ecosystem, that demand is rising fastest at spare parts & staging warehouses, which act as consolidation centers for components sourced from multiple OEMs for both the build out and the replenishment of spare parts, according to the report titled “Data Centers Drive Growth for Material Handling and Robotics.”
Over the longer term, investments in robotics within data centers themselves also hold a lot of potential, although it will likely remain unrealized in the short- to mid-term, given the complexity of the various tasks required.
Interact Analysis described four types of data centers: Hyperscale data centers are very large facilities operated by major cloud and internet companies; colocation facilities provide shared space, power, cooling and connectivity to multiple customers (broadly analogous to a third-party logistics model); enterprise data centers support the requirements of a single organization; and edge data centers are smaller facilities located closer to users and devices to reduce latency.
And finally, some additional logistics demand will also be generated by server integration facilities, which assemble, configure, and test complete server racks before shipping them to data centers, reducing on-site installation time and accelerating deployment and replacement cycles.

GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery . Here's an interesting case-study in using GPT-6.2 Astra for historical research, from history professor Mark Humphries:
With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library . It did so extremely quickly (in just 22 minutes), using publicly available primary and secondary sources. To do so, it discovered a little known source in a paper archive, predicted that it would prove its hypothesis if examined and, in the end, it did. Not only that, but this new source turns out to be a major find on its own that will be of significant interest to both Canadian and fur trade historians.
Astra found a diary reference reference to a visit by the vicomte de Chabot dated five days before a date mentioned in the sketchbook at a nearby river, and suggested that Chabot's journal of his travels (only available by order from Cleveland State University) might confirm that the sketchbook was his work.
Are historians due for a round of Deep Blue ? Mark thinks it will be mild:
But if the experience of mathematics is any guide, we can also anticipate that sometime next spring or summer we’ll face a sort of crisis of confidence as we struggle to understand how to respond to agentic systems that can do things human historians cannot. To be fair, that crisis will almost certainly be less profound for us than it is for math. The problem in mathematics, of course, is that solving hard math problems was the whole game. Historians, on the other hand, constantly reinterpret the past in light of an evolving present; we don’t chase a single universal truth. We also (in the ideal at least) write books and articles that are closer to works of philosophy and literature than they are to scientific tracts. Humanity is thus something of a requirement for the production of historical literature.

Refrigerated logistics is often assessed by warehouse capacity and trailer availability, but those measures describe infrastructure rather than delivered product integrity. A shipment may arrive on time yet have too little remaining shelf life, an unresolved temperature excursion or the wrong handling documentation. items.description: Anthropic 介绍如何将 Messages API 从 Python 迁移到 Rust，并把生产系统本身当作校验器。该 API 流量从 2024 年初到 2026 年秋增长约 1800 倍，迁移后每请求 CPU 降低约 70%，首 token 中位时间缩短约 20%，且未停服或冻结功能开发。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/h1ja45355xx1xf9rqf89cv1if
items.excerpt:
Anthropic 介绍如何将 Messages API 从 Python 迁移到 Rust，并把生产系统本身当作校验器。该 API 流量从 2024 年初到 2026 年秋增长约 1800 倍，迁移后每请求 CPU 降低约 70%，首 token 中位时间缩短约 20%，且未停服或冻结功能开发。
原文复盘了用生产系统当校验器迁移 API 的完整方法，读者可以借鉴定位和修复重写中的行为差异。
很多问题都存在 生成—验证 之间的落差：验证一个解法是否正确，往往比想出一个解法要容易得多。数独就是典型例子。检查答案很简单（只要数一数每行、每列、每个宫里的数字），但找到这个答案可能要花很长时间。许多雄心勃勃的 Claude 项目正是依赖这一落差：在数学中形式化 证明 ，或者 迁移 规模庞大、经过充分测试的代码库——只要 Claude 有可靠的办法验证自己的工作，这类任务它就能承担。
但随着 Claude 能力越来越强，它开始接手真实运行系统中的项目，而在这些系统里，生成工作反而比验证工作更容易。这类系统的用户常常依赖一些 不在测试套件覆盖范围内 的边界情况和特殊行为，而很难写出 一个能覆盖所有情况的“正确”定义 。没有可靠的办法检查 Claude 的工作，线上系统的迁移就很难让人放心——无论 Claude 生成代码有多快。
我们在把 Messages API 从 Python 迁移到 Rust 时就遇到了这个问题。这个 API 是客户以及我们自己的应用（比如 Claude Code 和 Cowork）访问 Claude 的主要途径。从 2024 年初到 2026 年秋，API 流量增长了约 1,800 倍。改用 Rust 后，每个请求消耗的 CPU 会少得多。Claude 用大约一周时间写出了这个 API 核心请求路径的第一版。但要让人信任这次迁移，我们必须找到一种办法，验证 Rust 版 API 与生产环境 API 行为一致。这件事之所以困难，原因有好几个：Python 版 API 在整个迁移过程中一直在变，所以“一致”是个不断移动的目标；Claude 对同一个请求的回复可能不确定，所以两份输出有差异不一定就是 bug；而且我们看不到客户的请求内容，也就无法轻易发现两个版本在哪里出现了分歧。
本文介绍我们如何把生产环境的 Messages API 本身变成一个验证器，以及这如何帮助我们在生产流量上测试新的 Rust 版本、找出两者的差异，并自动派发智能体去修复这些差异。最终我们上线了一个 Rust 版 API，每个请求消耗的 CPU 减少约 70%，首 token 中位延迟降低约 20%，而且全程没有让服务下线，也没有冻结功能开发。
我们在 2023 年构建了 Messages API，用 Python 编写，因为当时公司内部大量研究代码都用 Python。起初它很简单：Messages API 把请求转给模型，再把模型写出的内容发回去。（当时有位工程师称它“基本就是个请求转发器”。）但随着 Messages API 功能越来越强、与我们的代码库结合得越来越深，它也开始与研究团队和推理团队维护的 Python 库产生共享依赖，这让它很难挪动。如果哪天想换用另一种语言，就意味着日志、指标和工具全都要重新做一遍。
这种权衡逐渐开始改变。到 2025 年底，每个 Messages API 请求都必须经过校验、转换成提示词、分词，再由我们的安全分类器筛查。每收到一条回复，token 流都要被分拣成文本、思考和工具调用，而 Python 在每一步都会带来额外开销——每次创建对象、释放内存或把工作交给下一个任务时都是如此。流量最终远远超出了最初那个 Python 服务的设计承载能力（图 1），我们很快需要想办法让服务高效得多。
对大型生产系统做彻底重写，人们往往慎之又慎，至少有两个原因。第一，无法保证测试套件覆盖了生产代码 100% 的行为，重写有风险。第二，所需的工作量之大，常常让这种项目难以推进。（2024 年，我们一位工程师提出迁移到 Go 或 Rust 后，另一位工程师暂时给这个问题定了调：“ 我们不会用 go 或 rust 重写 API！ ”）
因此，想提升性能，通常的建议是只重写拖慢系统的那部分代码，我们也是从这里入手的。我们用 Rust 重写了负责解析模型输出的代码，并从 Python 调用它。这让 API 的 CPU 占用降低了约 8% 到 10%。不过，增量方案往往会带来额外的复杂度，因此必须确保增量改进值得付出这些代价。在我们的案例中，收益并不足以抵消增加的复杂度。现在每个 token 都要在 Python 和 Rust 之间来回穿越三次（图 2），又制造出新的开销来源。
增量重写之后，回复中的每个 token 都要在 Python 和 Rust 之间来回穿越三次。

items.title: When the Store Stops Stocking, the Distribution Network Inherits the Customer
items.description: When more retail locations sell from samples, distribution centers and delivery networks take responsibility for a larger share of the customer experience. The post When the Store Stops Stocking, the Distribution Network Inherits the Customer appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A retailer can remove a sofa from the store and free up a surprising amount of selling space. It cannot remove the sofa from the supply chain. The product still has to be stored, handled, loaded, delivered, and possibly returned. In fact, when a customer no longer takes possession at the store, the retailer assumes responsibility for a larger portion of the physical transaction.
That is the logistics consequence of showroom retail. The store may become a better place to sell, but the distribution network must become a better place to execute.
Traditional retail replenishment is built around relatively predictable destinations. A distribution center sends cases and pallets to known stores, often on consolidated routes. Merchandise is received, moved to the selling floor, and eventually carried away by the customer. Direct-to-consumer fulfillment is different. Individual orders leave on different days, travel to different addresses, and carry different service commitments. The basic unit of warehouse and transportation work changes.
There is no reason a retailer cannot manage both models. There is every reason not to assume the same network will handle both equally well.
Take a distribution center designed primarily to replenish stores. Its receiving, storage, picking, and shipping operations may be optimized for case quantities and stable store demand. A showroom-led network creates a different workload: each picking, item-level verification, protective packaging, carrier labeling, and order-specific dispatch.
The distinction sounds operational, but it changes the capital plan. Storage configuration, pick paths, sortation, packing stations, labor deployment, and automation choices depend on the order profile. So does the ability to accommodate peak demand. A warehouse that moves a high volume of cases efficiently may be poorly equipped to process thousands of small, variable orders with tight cutoff times.
Walmart’s October 8 announcement of its Stockton, California fulfillment center illustrates the scale of investment associated with customer-order fulfillment. The more than 900,000-square-foot facility uses automation and high-density storage to increase order capacity. Walmart described reducing a traditional 12-step fulfillment process to five steps. That is an operating-model investment, not simply a different place to keep merchandise.

items.description: Mass Spec Skills empowers scientists using Google Antigravity to interpret tandem mass spectra.
items.excerpt:
Robert Brunck, Stefan Ganscha, Swaroop Guntupalli, Dariusz Lasecki, Gabriella Marfani, Jack Mason, Hussain Masoom, Rose Mirshafian, Eliseo Papa and Zoi Tsangalidou
Built in collaboration with analytical chemists and using community-developed tools, Mass Spec Skills empowers scientists using Google Antigravity to interpret tandem mass spectra, lay out chemical evidence, and match frontier-level retrieval accuracy even with a lightweight model.
Every sample of blood, soil or plant tissue contains a vast array of small molecules, such as nutrients, hormones, drugs and their breakdown products, pollutants, or bioactive compounds with therapeutic potential. A modern mass spectrometer can detect tens of thousands of these molecular signals in a single drop of sample extract, measuring the masses of charged molecules and, in tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS), the fragments they break into.
These measurements, however, do not directly reveal the molecular structure. Researchers cannot immediately tell which compound produced a signal and relate it to its biological role or downstream use cases.
To fully map the diversity of small molecules, which remains largely uncharted, researchers need ways to translate mass spectra to molecular structures at scale. The standard approach is to match each spectrum against reference spectra from previously measured molecules. Yet even after a decade of expanding reference libraries, spectral searches annotate on average only about 5% of measured spectra, and 10% for human samples; the rest has been called the "dark matter" of mass spectrometry.
Many of the molecules producing these unannotated signals are already listed in public chemical databases, but their spectra have not been recorded, so there is no reference spectrum to compare against. Elucidating them instead requires inferring the structure directly from the observed fragment ions.
Analytical chemists have a well-tested, step-by-step workflow for narrowing down candidate structures from tandem (MS/MS) spectra: check spectral reference libraries, find the molecular formula and retrieve candidate structures from chemical databases, and then test every candidate against observed fragment peaks.

items.description: GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code. Lab tests found evidence of binding across five targets.
items.excerpt:
Our GPT‑6 family of models can design new protein shapes and the sequence of their chemical building blocks using only reasoning and code, without calling specialized biology models to generate those designs.
An internal research model matched or outperformed specialized models on many protein design tasks. Researchers could also guide designs by prompting the model on where a protein should attach and what shape it should take.
In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT‑6.2’s designs showed evidence of binding, or attachment, across five targets. Redesigned antibodies also retained binding. Specialized models helped supply sequences and select candidates for testing.
The models’ written reasoning and code suggest they draw on math, physics, chemistry, and biological knowledge to reason about protein shapes and interactions with other molecules.
In a preprint titled GPT‑6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models , we show that our GPT‑6 family of models has intrinsic capabilities for designing new proteins: the models can design new protein structures and sequences without relying on specialized biology models, using only reasoning and general-purpose coding tools.
Proteins do much of the work in living cells. They drive the chemical reactions that sustain life, carry oxygen through the blood, and defend the body against infection. Incorrectly shaped proteins can also cause disease and dysfunction. Proteins are made from chains of chemical building blocks called amino acids. The order, or sequence, of these amino acids helps determine how a protein folds into a three-dimensional shape, which in turn influences what it does.

They might want it to block a signal that helps cancer cells evade the immune system or to help capture carbon dioxide from the air. items.title: Intermodal’s Next Test Is Service Consistency, Not the Lowest Rate
items.description: Intermodal needs more than low rates. See why transit variability, drayage, terminal performance and inventory impacts determine durable modal conversion. The post Intermodal’s Next Test Is Service Consistency, Not the Lowest Rate appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Intermodal’s biggest commercial opportunity is not the occasional load that moves from highway to rail at a lower price. It is the freight that remains on intermodal because the service can be incorporated into inventory policy, production schedules and customer commitments. That requires a shift in measurement: from quoted linehaul cost and average transit time to dependable door-to-door performance and the economic cost of variation.
A rail linehaul is one part of an intermodal movement. The shipment begins with drayage, a terminal gate, and a train schedule; it ends with a second terminal, another truck, and a receiving appointment. Every transfer adds a chance of delay. Reliability is therefore not captured fully by train performance or a quoted transit time. A shipment can travel efficiently between terminals and still miss a customer deadline because chassis availability or appointment windows fail at the destination. Averages can also obscure variation: ten shipments arriving near plan may not offset one critical load that arrives after a production cutoff.
The opportunity is substantial. The Association of American Railroads reported that U.S. railroads averaged more than 298,000 intermodal units per week in October 2026, a monthly record for the weekly average. Volume strength demonstrates shipper interest in the mode, but aggregate demand is not a scorecard for every lane or shipment. A network operating near capacity may perform very differently at the origin terminal, on the mainline and in the destination drayage market. Shippers need to evaluate those segments separately before expanding commitments.
What matters most is the tail of the transit-time distribution. A lane that usually arrives in five days but occasionally requires nine can impose more inventory cost than one that reliably arrives in six. Replenishment orders, promotion calendars and manufacturing material requirements are sensitive to the late shipment, not to the average shipment. That is why planners should compare performance at the 90th or 95th percentile alongside median transit time, missed appointments, container availability and recovery after a missed connection.
